title: incident-bot: streamline on-call autodiagnostics workflow and SLO-toolkit utilities
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: On-call engineers frequently run a standard set of diagnostics and consult runbooks/SLO hints during incidents. The current incident-bot flow surfaces runbook links and basic SLO hints but requires manual orchestration for multi-step diagnostics. This PR centralizes the autodiagnostics workflow, augments SLO-toolkit utilities with richer hint scoring, and adds small UX/telemetry improvements for on-call helpers.

What this changes: 1) New autodiag workflow orchestration that sequences lightweight checks (service status, recent deploys, error-rate snapshots, KV-cache health) and surfaces prioritized runbook links with confidence scores. 2) SLO-toolkit: add hint-scoring functions and heuristics used to rank runbooks and suggested actions. 3) Runbook templates: compact diagnostic entry added for common infra issues. 4) On-call helpers: improved ephemeral context payloads and rate-limited suggestions to reduce chat spam. 5) Add end-to-end tests and telemetry events for sampling and ranking results.

Implementation notes: - incident-bot/src/autodiag/workflow.py: implements the orchestrator with pluggable check modules and a simple retry/backoff for flaky sources. - slo-toolkit/src/hints.py: new scoring surface (heuristics + signal weights) and cumulative confidence output. - incident-bot/runbooks/compact_diagnostic.md: compact runbook template used by autodiag. - incident-bot/api/context_payload.py: reduced payload size for ephemeral on-call suggestions; added a TTL field. - tests/integration/test_autodiag_flow.py: synthetic scenario tests covering SLO-based ranking and runbook linking.

Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for scoring heuristics - [x] Integration tests for end-to-end autodiag flow - [x] Telemetry events emitted for ranking and chosen actions - [x] Docs updated with short how-to for on-call use - [x] Feature gated behind FF_ONCALL_AUTODIAG

Rollout plan: feature is gated. Will enable for a small subset of SRE users (beta group) for 48 hours, collect telemetry (rank stability, chosen runbooks, suggestion acceptance), then widen rollout if no regressions. Backout: toggle FF_ONCALL_AUTODIAG=false.

Backward compatibility: All public incident-bot endpoints unchanged. New SLO-toolkit helpers are additive. The reduced context payload is opt-in via a header for callers; incident-bot continues to accept old payload shapes for a 2-week migration window.

Notes on performance: The autodiag orchestrator parallelizes remote calls where safe and applies a 2s soft timeout per external data source to preserve on-call latency goals. Expected median latency for a full autodiag run is ~600-900ms (measured in integration tests under synthetic conditions).

Related: ENG-2021 (oncall autodiag epic), SRE-314 (runbook prioritization), SUP-8821 (customer-reported oncall friction).
